history.summary: CSV TOWN CORRECTION (flagged): the famous Barunei Temple is NOT in Mayurbhanj — it stands on Barunei Hill in Khordha district, ~30 km from Bhubaneswar (state Odisha, correcting the CSV 'state' field which wrongly repeats the town name). It is one of Odisha's Shakti Pithas, dedicated to the twin goddesses Barunei and Karunei (manifestations of Shakti) — black-granite (Kalamuguni pathara) idols in warrior dress, the hill itself named for the goddess; the sacred Swarna Ganga stream flows from the hill. One source credits King Ramachandra Dev of Khordha with the temple; a weaker travel source claims 800+ years and a Paramara king. Barunei Hill is historically significant as the site of the 1817 Paika Rebellion — Paika soldiers used the temple and hills as hideouts, and monuments/inscriptions around the temple commemorate the revolt. Folklore also links the hill to the Pandavas (Pandaba Guha, Pandaba Cave, Shri Rama Pathara) and a stream Sita blessed never to run dry.
